paragraph: These images from Cluster 0 consistently present pigmented skin lesions characterized by a spectrum of brown hues, ranging from light brown to very dark brown, almost black, against a lighter skin background where fine hairs are often visible. A primary common feature is the presence of architectural irregularity in both their internal structure and peripheral borders. While the first image shows a generally rounded to oval lesion with an internal reticular pattern and somewhat wavy, but mostly defined borders, the second lesion exhibits marked asymmetry and highly irregular, often spiky or pseudopod-like extensions radiating from a denser, darker central core. Despite these variations in the degree and type of irregularity, both lesions share significant pigment heterogeneity and a clear tendency towards irregular borders and internal patterns, suggesting their classification as melanocytic lesions with varying degrees of atypical features, making this combination of brown pigmentation and structural irregularity a distinctive hallmark of this cluster.
